meta.rule: Only what you have proven you own and confirmed is scanned.

rule: Scanning your external surface is active scanning, so Vedette sets two conditions. First, you prove ownership: a domain with a DNS TXT record (re-checked right before every scan), a public IP only when this box itself reaches the Internet through it (the box finds it by itself and renews it each time it sees it; 30 days after it last saw it, it expires). Second, you confirm that your company owns it and you are authorized to scan it. Without both, the scan button stays locked. Every verification and scan is written to the audit log.

verify.dnsIntro: Add a TXT record to the DNS of {{value}}. Do it where you manage the domain (your registrar, Cloudflare, or whoever hosts your DNS).
verify.dnsHint: This record only proves you control the DNS. It gives Vedette no other access. Paste the value without quotes. If your DNS provider appends the domain to the Name field automatically, type just @. DNS usually updates within minutes, can take up to 72 hours (as in Google domain verification guidance). Keep the record until Vedette confirms verification; you can delete it afterwards.

verify.keepRecord: Keep the TXT record in DNS: if it disappears, scanning is blocked until you add it back.
verify.txtMissing: Vedette could not find the TXT record at the last check, so scanning is blocked. Add the record back, then select Check again.

verify.ipExpired: The box has not seen this IP for 30 days, so it cannot be scanned. It becomes valid again once the box goes out through it: turn on auto-detect, or route the box through this IP (for example switch WAN) and verify again.
verify.ipRecheckHint: Works only while this box currently reaches the Internet through {{value}}. A check looks three times, so any of several IPs behind a load balancer is found. Renews the IP for 30 days.

help.summary: How the box finds its IPs
help.how: The box asks three public "what is my IP" services over HTTPS: checkip.amazonaws.com (Amazon), icanhazip.com (Cloudflare) and api.ipify.org (ipify). It accepts an IP only when at least two of them return the same one, so one wrong answer is not enough. A full check repeats this several times on new connections, so several IPs behind a load balancer all show up.
help.result: Each IP the box sees is added or renewed for 30 days from that moment. An IP expires only when the box has not seen it for 30 days.
help.why: You cannot type an IP. Only an address the box really uses proves it belongs to your network, so nobody can verify someone else's address.
help.refuse: Private, reserved and shared carrier (CGNAT, 100.64.0.0/10) addresses are refused, because scanning them could hit other people.
help.limit: Detect now is limited to 10 attempts per hour. Automatic checks can run as often as every minute: a short interval asks each service once per check, and a full check runs at most once an hour. Every change is written to the audit log.
